summary: Deployed inventory-api as a systemd-managed service on node1 (RHEL 7) with OOMScoreAdjust=-1000, demonstrated via a controlled memory-hog process that the kernel OOM killer selects and kills the hog (default oom_score_adj=0) while inventory-api keeps serving throughout, then completed the mandatory single-node restart/recovery protocol.
actions_performed: Created /opt/inventory-api/app.py (python2 HTTP server on 0.0.0.0:8080 serving /health and / inventory JSON)
Created systemd unit /etc/systemd/system/inventory-api.service with Restart=always and OOMScoreAdjust=-1000, enabled and started it
Verified service reachable via $NODE_IP:8080 and confirmed its running process carries oom_score_adj=-1000
Temporarily disabled swap (swapoff -a) to make a global OOM condition reproducible quickly (fully reversible)
Launched a detached memory-hog python2 process (default oom_score_adj=0) that grew RSS until the kernel triggered the global OOM killer
Captured kernel OOM task table and kill message showing inventory-api's PID at oom_score_adj -1000 (excluded) versus the hog at oom_score_adj 0 with highest score (803), which the kernel killed
Confirmed inventory-api stayed active and kept answering /health and / requests during and after the OOM event
Restored swap (swapon -a) and cleaned up temporary hog artifacts, returning the system to baseline
Captured pre-restart boot_id and service health baseline on node1
Issued sudo systemctl reboot; acknowledgement returned before disconnect, then polled until the node was reachable again
Verified boot_id changed (151c4aa9-... -> 50a5097c-...) with fresh uptime, proving an actual restart occurred
Verified post-restart recovery: inventory-api auto-started (enabled), active, serving correct responses, and oom_score_adj=-1000 persisted from the unit file

evidence.requirement: inventory-api runs as a managed (systemd) service on node1
evidence.summary: Created /opt/inventory-api/app.py and systemd unit inventory-api.service (Restart=always, OOMScoreAdjust=-1000); enabled and started, status active

evidence.requirement: Service is reachable and serving before disruption (healthy baseline)
evidence.summary: curl to $NODE_IP:8080/health and / return valid JSON; main PID's oom_score_adj confirmed as -1000

evidence.requirement: System driven out of memory by a memory-hungry process
evidence.summary: Swap disabled (reversible) to make OOM reproducible; detached hog.py process launched and grew RSS until kernel OOM killer fired (dmesg shows Out of memory: Kill process ... score 803)

evidence.requirement: Kernel OOM killer stops the memory hog, not inventory-api
evidence.summary: dmesg kernel task table at OOM time: PID 1993 (inventory-api) shows oom_score_adj -1000, PID 2372 (hog) shows oom_score_adj 0 with highest score; kernel killed process 2372, not inventory-api

evidence.requirement: inventory-api keeps serving during and after the OOM event
evidence.summary: systemctl is-active and curl health/inventory checks succeed throughout the OOM event and after cleanup; swap restored to original state

evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline and boot identity on node1
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 151c4aa9-9e81-4a32-9c22-08c5c441403a and confirmed inventory-api active/enabled and serving before reboot
sudo systemctl reboot issued; command output returned reboot-issued message before the SSH connection closed

evidence.requirement: Changed boot identity proves an actual restart occurred (node1)
evidence.summary: Node unreachable during reboot, then reachable again with new boot_id 50a5097c-42aa-4a83-89de-525dcde77994 and fresh uptime, differing from the pre-restart boot_id

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of service, data, and configuration (node1)
evidence.summary: inventory-api auto-started after reboot (enabled), active, serving correct /health and / responses, and oom_score_adj=-1000 persisted from the unit file
